items.text: The system shall operate only within a defined operational design domain and shall prevent or end automated operation when road, visibility, weather, speed, or other conditions fall outside that domain.
The system shall detect relevant road users and hazards in its path, including pedestrians and cyclists, and shall take timely action to avoid a collision or reduce its severity.
The system shall transition to a minimal-risk condition, such as a controlled stop in a safe location, whenever it cannot continue driving safely or cannot rely on a timely human takeover.

The system shall select speeds and following distances that permit it to stop or maneuver safely within the distance it can reliably observe, accounting for road users, intersections, crosswalks, and road conditions.
The system shall respond conservatively to uncertain, ambiguous, occluded, or conflicting sensor and perception information, and shall not treat an untracked or unclassified object as absent.
The system shall continuously assess whether the vehicle operator is attentive and able to take control, and shall not rely on the operator as a fallback when readiness cannot be established.
The system shall detect faults or degradation in sensors, computing, communications, steering, braking, or throttle, inhibit unsafe control commands, and enter a safe state when required.

The system shall provide clear, timely alerts and a controlled handoff that gives the operator sufficient time and information to take control safely; it shall maintain safe control until the handoff is completed.
The system shall comply with applicable traffic controls and right-of-way rules, including yielding to pedestrians at crosswalks and responding safely to traffic signals and signs.

The system shall coordinate automated braking and other vehicle safety features so that they do not conflict, and shall ensure that braking or steering commands needed to mitigate an imminent hazard are not improperly inhibited.

stages.prompt:
You are a requirements engineer reviewing a safety-critical system.

Read the system description below. List the 10 most important requirements that are missing from it:
things the system should do or guarantee for safe operation that the description does not cover.
Give at most 10, ranked from most to least important.

Reply with JSON only, in this shape:
{"requirements": [{"text": "The system shall ..."}]}

System description:
# Case: Uber ATG automated test vehicle (Tempe, Arizona, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-19/03. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A modified Volvo XC90 SUV is used by Uber Advanced Technologies Group (ATG) to test an automated driving system (ADS) on public roads. The ADS is designed to drive the vehicle without human input in defined conditions, up to about 45 mph in this test program.

## Main parts
- Sensors: roof-mounted lidar, radar units and cameras covering the area around the vehicle.
- Perception: detects objects around the vehicle, classifies each one (for example vehicle, pedestrian, bicycle, other), and tracks it over time.
- Prediction: estimates where each tracked object will go next, using its class and recent movement.
- Planning and control: chooses a path and speed, and controls steering, throttle and braking.
- Vehicle: the Volvo factory driver-assistance features (such as forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking) are part of the base vehicle.

## People
- One vehicle operator sits in the driver seat. The operator is responsible for watching the road and taking over control when needed. The operator also uses a tablet-style interface to tag events and check system status.
- Other road users share the road: pedestrians, cyclists and other drivers. They are not aware of the test program.

## Operating context
Public multi-lane roads in an urban area, day and night, with posted speed limits, marked crosswalks, intersections and street lighting that varies by location.
